messages:
incident-bot: Pager: SLA_BREACH: tenant=ozark, error_rate_5xx=6.8% over 5m, alerts fired (pager). Severity: P2. Link: https://grafana.redwood/alert/ozark-sla

alice_oncall: I'm on it. looking at traces now, pulling up recent deploys.

ben_sre: i can take metrics + infra side. alice, can you check model/routing side for any sudden increase in 5xx?

alice_oncall: on it — first glance: there's a small spike in failed responses from cluster-inference-us-west-2-3, started ~10:00 UTC. no deploys in last 30m.

carla_prod: customer rachel_pm flagged latency and errors via support earlier. looks like errors correlate with a tenant-specific throttling check (ozark) we recently added.

rachel_pm: confirmation from Ozark: they saw a wave of request retries and some SLA page hits on their side. They say it started around 09:58 UTC.

tom_support: I have the support thread open, relaying to Ozark they might see intermittent 5xx > 5% — asking for request ids.

ben_sre: running quick agg query:
```
# prometheus-like psuedoquery
sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="ozark",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="ozark"}[5m])) * 100
```
Result: 6.3% at peak across replicas. cluster-inference-us-west-2-3 shows 12% locally.

alice_oncall: traced a failing path: prefix KV cache miss -> fallback to slow path -> upstream timeout -> 502. Looks like a specific cache key shape coming from ozark's traffic pattern.

jorge_platform: We can throttle and route ozark traffic to a lower-concurrency pool temporarily to avoid cascading failures. But that may increase latency.

alice_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) add ozark to watchlist and silence noisy cross-tenant alert; 2) create temporary routing rule to steer ozark to warm pool; 3) tune alert evaluation to reduce paging noise while we stabilize.

ben_sre: agreed. also add a dashboard panel for ozark 5xx by node. I'll spin up a grafana panel.

ops-bot: action created: INCIDENT-5782 "Ozark tenant SLA spike - live mitigation" assigned to alice_oncall, ben_sre; due: 1832180000.

alice_oncall: doing manual routing change now — executing:
```bash
# route ozark to warm pool (one-off)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CFG" https://api.redwood/internal/routing -d '{"tenant":"ozark","pool":"warm-pool-usw2-3","priority":10}'
```

alice_oncall: route applied. monitoring.

ben_sre: i've added temporary dashboard panel and a heatmap for 5xx per node: https://grafana.redwood/d/ozark-5xx-heatmap

carla_prod: to reduce pager noise: propose adjusting the tenant-level SLA alert rule: change threshold from 5% to 7% for 5m window OR keep 5% but require 2/3 eval windows (5m -> 3 evaluations = 15m). which do we prefer?

rachel_pm: prefer shorter window so we can catch real regressions quickly, so leaning to 7% for now with a follow-up to evaluate proper baselining. Ozark is impacted but agreed we shouldn't page every transient blip.

ben_sre: technical note: increasing threshold to 7% reduces sensitivity but avoids noisy pages from cache-warmups. alternative is to add a suppression rule that only pages if node-level >10% sustained 3 evals.

alice_oncall: I'm going to patch the alert temporarily:
```yaml
alert: TenantSLAHigh5xx_Ozark
expr: (sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="ozark",status=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{tenant="ozark"}[5m]))) * 100 > 7
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Ozark SLA 5xx > 7% (temporary)"
```
Applying now.

ops-bot: deploy: alert-rule-update succeeded (change id: ar-5532) by alice_oncall at 1832111205.

alice_oncall: alert updated. paging suppressed for current blip; still tracking errors.

tom_support: Ozark confirmed they see decreased error volume after ~10:12 UTC. they still want postmortem.

ben_sre: i pushed a small hotfix to inference runtime to add a backoff on KV cache miss path; rolling to two nodes first.

ben_sre: rolling update logs: node-3 took longer to replace, saw transient 502s — but overall error rate dropped after second node healthy.

rachel_pm: customer-facing note: I'll craft an initial message to Ozark explaining mitigation and next steps.

carla_prod: follow-up actions (captured):
- Create a tenant-specific dashboard (ben) ✅
- Re-evaluate alert thresholds with historical baseline (alice + carla) — ticket created: PM-1445
- Add a guardrail to routing rules to avoid fallback storms (jorge)
- Add unit test in runtime for KV cache miss path (ben)
- Postmortem with RCA and timeline (alice)

alice_oncall: logging timeline into INCIDENT-5782, setting follow-up meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC.

ops-bot: comment added to INCIDENT-5782: "Alert threshold temporarily raised from 5% -> 7% for tenant ozark. Remember to revert or set a permanent rule after postmortem."

ben_sre: one more thought — we should consider alert noise classification tags: add `noisy-tenant` tag to alerts that are allowed higher thresholds in the next sprint. I'll raise a PR for alert taxonomy.

alice_oncall: thanks everyone. i'll keep monitoring and will post RCA draft in #postmortems once we have logs. closing the page for now but keeping watch. :white_check_mark: 

tom_support: marking support ticket as "monitoring - mitigation applied" and asking ozark to confirm stability in 30m.

rachel_pm: annotated in customer notes. we'll sync on the postmortem scope tomorrow.

jorge_platform: follow-up infra task created: INFRA-2309 "Routing guardrail: prevent full-fallback storms for single-tenant bursts".

alice_oncall: last update: current 5xx for ozark 1.2% over 5m. closing thread, will reopen if it flares.
